2027-03-20.title: Sixth Saturday of the Great Fast
2027-03-20.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
2027-03-20.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba). Tomorrow is Hosanna Sunday, and the Week of the Passion begins.
2027-03-20.verse: The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
theo: On the eve of Hosanna Sunday the Church sets two farewells side by side. Paul is on his way to Jerusalem and calls the elders of Ephesus to Miletus. He knows what is coming: “And now, as a captive to the Spirit, I am on my way to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there, except that the Holy Spirit testifies to me in every city that imprisonment and persecutions are waiting for me.” He is not afraid: “But I do not count my life of any value to myself, if only I may finish my course and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify to the good news of God's grace.” He charges the elders to shepherd “the church of God that he obtained with the blood of his own Son”, and gives them a saying of Jesus found nowhere else in Scripture: “It is more blessed to give than to receive.” Then “he knelt down with them all and prayed. There was much weeping among them all; they embraced Paul and kissed him.” Paul walks toward Jerusalem as his Master did, with his face set and his heart full of love for those he leaves behind. Every priest who has left a parish, every parent who has watched a child leave for a distant country, knows something of that shore at Miletus.

The Gospel takes us to Bethany “six days before the Passover”. Lazarus, raised from the dead, sits at the table; Martha serves, as she always does; and Mary does something no one expected. She “took a pound of costly perfume made of pure nard, anointed Jesus' feet, and wiped them with her hair. The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.” A pound of pure nard was worth a year's wages. Judas objects that it should have been sold for the poor, but John tells us his heart was not with the poor. Jesus defends her: “Leave her alone. She bought it so that she might keep it for the day of my burial.” Mary has understood what the disciples have not: that he is going to die, and that love does not calculate at such a moment. Her gift is extravagant, and the whole house is filled with it. Tomorrow we will wave palms and cry Hosanna; this evening the Gospel asks what we will pour out at his feet in the coming week. In many homes the days before Pesaha are spent cleaning the house and preparing for the Pesaha appam. Let the house be filled too with the fragrance of prayer, forgiveness and generous love.

live: With your family, make the house ready for the Week of the Passion: a cleaned prayer corner, a cross in its place, the television quieter.
Give one gift this week that costs you something, without calculating.
2027-03-20.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, six days before the Passover you sat at table in Bethany, and Mary poured out her costly perfume at your feet. Give us her love that does not calculate, and Paul's courage to finish the course. As we enter the Week of your Passion, fill our homes with the fragrance of prayer and generous love. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the Lord whose body Mary anointed for burial gives that same body to us, risen and glorious; the Church obtained by his blood is gathered at his table.

quick: Paul goes to Jerusalem as a captive to the Spirit, counting his life of no value.
It is more blessed to give than to receive.
Mary pours out her perfume, and the whole house is filled with its fragrance.
2027-03-20.action: Give one gift this week that costs you something.
2027-03-20.question: What will I pour out at the feet of Jesus in the coming week?

family.explain: Jesus went to visit his friends Martha, Mary and Lazarus. During dinner Mary took a jar of very expensive perfume and poured it on Jesus' feet, and the whole house smelled beautiful. She loved Jesus so much that she gave him her very best.
family.intention: We pray for our family as we get ready for Hosanna Sunday and the Week of the Passion.
family.ask: Ask: “What is the best thing we can give to Jesus this week?”

illus: In a parish in Changanassery, an elderly widow brought a small bottle of attar to the sacristy on the Saturday before Hosanna Sunday every year. Her husband had brought it back from the Gulf the year before he died, and she used a drop each year on the linen for the altar of repose on Pesaha. The sacristan once asked why she did not keep it for herself. “It was the most precious thing he gave me,” she said. “Where else should it go?” For a whole evening every Pesaha, the side chapel smelled of that bottle.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, we sit with you at table, as Mary, Martha and Lazarus did. Receive what we bring. Amen.
share: I do not count my life of any value to myself, if only I may finish my course (Acts 20:24). What course has God given me to finish?
It is more blessed to give than to receive (Acts 20:35). When did I last give without counting the cost?
The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume (John 12:3). What would fill my home with the fragrance of Christ this week?
interc: For the Church as she enters the Week of the Passion.
For pastors, that they may shepherd the flock obtained by Christ's blood.
For missionaries and all who have left home for the Gospel.
For the poor, who are always with us.
For our group, that our love for Christ may be generous.
pm.close: Father, as your Son came to Bethany six days before the Passover, he comes to our homes. Fill them with the fragrance of love, and make us generous at his feet. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul tells the elders of Ephesus that he is going to Jerusalem as a captive to the Spirit. Prison and persecution wait for him. Yet he says: I do not count my life of any value to myself, if only I may finish my course (Acts 20:24).
He reminds them of a word of the Lord Jesus: it is more blessed to give than to receive (Acts 20:35). Then they kneel together, weep and embrace him on the shore.

Six days before the Passover, Mary of Bethany pours a pound of costly nard on Jesus' feet and wipes them with her hair. The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume (John 12:3). Jesus says she has kept it for the day of his burial.
Tomorrow we wave palms and cry Hosanna. Tonight let us ask what we will pour out at his feet this week. Let our homes be filled with the fragrance of prayer and love. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary gave Jesus her most precious perfume, and the whole house smelled lovely. What is something special you can give to Jesus this week? Maybe your time in prayer, or a kind act for someone at home.

intro: Theme: “The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.”
Paul's farewell on the way to Jerusalem, and Mary's extravagant love on the eve of the Passion.

q: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his faithful ones.
But I do not count my life of any value to myself, if only I may finish my course and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify to the good news of God’s grace.
points.apply: Name the course God has given you to finish, and take one step on it this week.

sub: The flock obtained by his blood.
q: Since there will never cease to be some in need on the earth, I therefore command you, “Open your hand to the poor and needy neighbor in your land.”
In all this I have given you an example that by such work we must support the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus, for he himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’
points.apply: Give one gift this week that costs you something.

sub: Kept for the day of his burial.
q: your anointing oils are fragrant, your name is perfume poured out; therefore the maidens love you.
Mary took a pound of costly perfume made of pure nard, anointed Jesus’ feet, and wiped them with her hair. The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
points.apply: Prepare your home with your family for the Week of the Passion, and fill it with prayer.

concl: Paul and Mary both know that Jesus is going to his death, and both answer with love that does not calculate.
Tomorrow we cry Hosanna; this week let us pour out our best at his feet.
2027-03-20.resolve: Prepare the house for the Week of the Passion, and give one costly gift without counting.
